data.title: Good design makes itself felt.
data.lede: A creative studio for brands, spaces and culture. We design with intention and craft lasting impressions.

hero_image.alt: A folded sheet of off-white paper curling into a sculptural form, with a bright orange underside

data.title: A small studio that stays close to the work.
data.lede: Forma is a fictional design studio used to demonstrate this theme. We work across identity, packaging, spaces and art direction, and keep teams small so the people who scope a project are the people who make it.

hero_image.alt: Curved concrete walls meeting under a pale evening sky, with a warm orange recess

children.text: How we began

Forma started as two designers sharing a table and a habit of asking why before asking how. The studio has grown slowly since, adding people when a project needed a new kind of thinking rather than more hands.
Every project begins with a conversation about the problem, not the deliverables. We would rather spend an extra week understanding a brief than a month refining the wrong answer.
Who we work with

Founders shaping a first identity, cultural organisations opening a new space, and established teams who want an outside eye on something they care about. If the work matters to you, it will matter to us.

points.title: Brief first
points.text: We agree on the problem and how we will judge the answer before we draw anything.

points.title: Material honesty
points.text: Paper, concrete, light and type are chosen for what they are, not dressed up as something else.

points.title: Small teams
points.text: The people in the first meeting stay on the project until it is delivered.

points.title: Room to breathe
points.text: Generous space in layouts and in schedules leaves room for better decisions.

data.title: AKA
data.summary: A calm, tactile identity and packaging range for a fictional skincare label built around the idea of a quieter tomorrow.

featured_image.alt: Two textured off-white AKA boxes on a rough stone plinth beside a dark rock and a sprig of dried orange flowers

data.deliverables: Naming support, identity, packaging range, art direction

children.text: AKA wanted to launch a small range of evening skincare without the loud claims and glossy finishes common to the category. The founders asked for packaging that felt like an object worth keeping on a shelf, and an identity that could stay quiet without disappearing.
We started with materials rather than logos. Uncoated, textured board set the tone, and the wordmark was drawn as three upright letters that read like a label on a specimen box.
A single line of copy, “A quieter tomorrow”, carries the brand idea across every pack. Colour is reserved for the products themselves, so the boxes stay neutral and the range reads as one family.

The finished system covers the identity, a four-product packaging range, shipping materials and a photography direction built on stone, shadow and dried botanicals. The studio delivered print-ready artwork and a short guide so the in-house team can extend the range.

image.alt: Close view of the AKA box and the smaller box printed with the line A quieter tomorrow

gallery.caption: The two core formats share one stock and one typographic voice.

image.alt: A dark volcanic stone resting against a textured box

gallery.caption: Props were chosen to echo the surface of the board.

image.alt: A sprig of dried orange flowers against a black backdrop

gallery.caption: Dried botanicals bring the only warm colour into the set.

data.title: Solace
data.summary: A retreat house shaped by curved concrete, still water and a single warm room at its centre.

featured_image.alt: A curved concrete wall beside a dark reflecting pool and an olive tree, with an orange-lit doorway

data.deliverables: Spatial concept, material palette, interior direction

children.text: The owners of a small plot in a dry landscape asked for a house that would feel cool in summer, sheltered in winter and quiet all year. They wanted a place to slow down, not a statement.

We worked with the project architect on the spatial concept and material palette. A curved concrete volume wraps the bedrooms, a shallow pool cools the courtyard air, and a single room finished in warm plaster marks the centre of the house.
Openings are deep and few, so light arrives in measured amounts and moves across the walls through the day.

The concept, palette and interior direction were delivered as a set of drawings, samples and reference boards that guided construction. The client team now uses the same palette for furniture and landscaping decisions.

gallery.caption: The curved volume shades the courtyard through the afternoon.

image.alt: A tall doorway glowing orange inside a concrete wall

gallery.caption: The warm room is visible from the entrance path.

image.alt: An olive tree in front of the concrete facade

gallery.caption: Existing olive trees were kept and framed by the plan.

data.title: Fold
data.summary: A paper installation and campaign for a fictional paper mill, showing what a single sheet can become.

featured_image.alt: A large sheet of off-white paper folded into a twisting sculpture with an orange inner face

data.deliverables: Concept, installation design, art direction, campaign imagery

children.text: Halden wanted to introduce a new two-tone stock to designers and printers. Rather than a swatch book, they asked for something that would show the paper's strength, colour and surface at a scale people would remember.

We built a single continuous sheet into a self-supporting form, letting the orange reverse appear only where the paper turns. Models were folded by hand at small scale, then enlarged and tested with the mill's production team.
The same form was photographed against a plain studio backdrop to become the campaign image, so the installation and the printed material tell one story.
The installation, a set of campaign photographs and a printed sample folder were delivered for the stock launch. Templates for the folder were handed over so Halden can produce new editions in-house.

image.alt: Close-up of the orange underside of the paper twisting between pale folds

gallery.caption: The orange reverse appears only where the sheet turns.

image.alt: Detail of pale paper curves overlapping in soft light

gallery.caption: Surface texture is visible at close range.

data.title: Threshold
data.summary: Wayfinding and a small identity for a fictional gallery set inside a former concrete works.

featured_image.alt: A curved concrete wall leading to an entrance lined in warm orange

children.text: A new gallery in a former concrete works needed visitors to find the entrance, move between rooms and understand what was on show, without adding visual noise to raw, heavy spaces.

We used colour as the main wayfinding device: every public threshold is lined in the same warm orange, visible from across the site. Signs are kept to a minimum and set in one typeface at a small number of sizes.
The identity, signage family and a placement plan were delivered with fabrication drawings. Gallery staff can update exhibition titles using the supplied templates.

image.alt: A tall doorway glowing orange inside a concrete wall

gallery.caption: Every public threshold is lined in the same warm orange.

image.alt: Concrete walls curving under a pale sky

gallery.caption: Signs stay small so the building can speak first.

data.title: Ember Notes
data.summary: Still-life photography for a fictional tea company's autumn collection, built from stone, shadow and dried flowers.

featured_image.alt: Dried orange flowers on a slender stem against a black background

children.text: Ember asked for a small set of images for an autumn collection that would feel warm without relying on the usual props of steam, cups and leaves.
We kept the palette to black, stone and one warm accent. Each frame uses a single object and hard side light, so the images can sit next to each other as a series.
A series of still-life images was delivered for web, print and in-store use, with a short guide describing the lighting and set so future seasons can follow the same approach.

image.alt: A dark stone in hard side light

gallery.caption: One object, one light source per frame.
The warm accent carries across the series.
